title: Optimizing Long-tailed Link Prediction in Graph Neural Networks through Structure Representation Enhancement

problem.claim: GNN link prediction is hindered by a long-tailed distribution of node pairs with few common neighbors, which perform worse.

gap.claim: The effect of degree-based long-tailed structure on GNN link prediction and the role of common neighbors require investigation.

contributions.claim: Common-neighbor count has a stronger correlation with predictive accuracy than node degree.
LTLP enhances tail node-pair link prediction by increasing common neighbors through edge supplementation and representational alignment.
Across five datasets, LTLP is reported to achieve SOTA performance and reduce performance bias between head and tail node pairs.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The study reports only a mild correlation between node degree and predictive accuracy.
Empirical results across five datasets are reported to show SOTA performance and reduced head-tail performance bias.

narrative_sequence.summary: Link prediction is a fundamental GNN task whose success is influenced by node representation.
The study finds that common-neighbor count, more than node degree, correlates with predictive accuracy, exposing a long-tailed problem among node pairs.
LTLP addresses the problem by increasing common neighbors and aligning representations between head and tail node pairs.
Results across five datasets are reported to show strong performance and reduced bias between head and tail pairs.

unknowns: The five datasets, evaluation metrics, baselines, and numerical results are unspecified.
The procedures for supplementing edges and enforcing representational alignment are unspecified.
The abstract does not provide independent verification or detailed experimental conditions.
